title: Telos-native joint generator versus matched sequential and conventional inference
status: proposed protocol; not frozen, not run, no result
purpose: Test whether coupled endogenous resource/geometry/interrogation/memory/morphogenesis dynamics improve downstream distinctions at matched viability and compute, separately from exact CTMC order-independence.

scope.organism: finite synthetic Worldlets and two geometric candidates only
scope.environment: withheld-context switch, appearance recoding, response noise and drift; no hidden semantics given to learner
scope.previous_results: all G0-AB, G0-AC and G0-Y artifacts are frozen and remain unchanged

comparators: Lie-Trotter stage-split approximation with decreasing timestep
real-valued capacity- and history-matched context estimator
static morphology and static interrogation ablations
invariants: invariance under independent GL(4) frame reexpression
generator probability normalization and nonnegative offdiagonal
metrics: false equivalence rate conditioned on attempted declarations
false buds and valid bud recoveries
recovery under drift and context changes
actual CPU wall and peak traced memory
parity: Match sensing observations, history access, data, capacity, structure budgets, random seed streams, CPU/memory where practical; equal caps are not equal spend
kill_rules: No cognitive advantage claim if conventional estimator ties or wins at comparable resource cost and coverage
No concurrency benefit claim if splitting converges to same joint process as timestep decreases
No useful morphology claim if bud precision is insufficient or improves only on leaked labels
No special geometry claim if chart-aware real implementation ties
Never infer quantum advantage from a diagonal Lindblad embedding
availability: CPU-only, stdlib-only, no GPU, no network access from model, no external job scheduling
authority: Generated or validated tests do not self-promote claims: only independent held-out witness may change H to M
